title.value: Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus on improving evaluation methodologies for offline and online reinforcement learning.
title.quote: Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies

extractions.description: This paper proposes a sequential evaluation methodology for offline reinforcement learning algorithms, emphasizing data efficiency and robustness to distribution changes. It compares various offline RL algorithms and introduces practical applications like offline-to-online transitions, using benchmarks such as D4RL and DMC.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving reinforcement learning methodologies without a direct focus on climate change themes.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this paper, we propose a sequential approach to evaluate offline RL algorithms as a function of the training set size and thus by their data efficiency.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any specific climate change issues or themes directly. Its focus is on reinforcement learning evaluation methodologies.
primary_category.quote: While online RL algorithms are typically evaluated as a function of the number of environment interactions, there isn’t a single established protocol for evaluating offline RL methods.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the primary category is 'N/A', the sub-category is also not applicable due to the lack of direct relevance to climate change topics.
primary_sub_category.quote: These algorithms were evaluated on the D4RL benchmark (Fu et al., 2020), which consists of three environments: Halfcheetah-v2, Walker2d-v2 and Hopper-v2.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce any new categories relevant to climate change as it does not focus on this area.
new_primary_category.quote: We compare several existing offline RL algorithms using this approach and present insights from a variety of tasks and offline datasets.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There are no new sub-categories introduced that relate to climate change within the focus of this paper.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our approach is generally applicable and easy to implement.
